---
title: Sharing Checks in a Package
toc-expand: 2
bread-crumbs: true
---

This guide shows you how to distribute check collections (and options for the other config
groups) in a Python package. Anyone who installs the package can select them in a
[composed configuration](hydra-composition.qmd), with no setup in their own project.

The package needs a directory of config files and an entry point that tells Hydra where that
directory is. It can also have Python code for the collections to use.

## Lay Out the Config Tree

Put the config files in a directory inside your package, arranged by config group. Within each
group, put them in a directory named after your package or organization (`acme/` here), so that
your options can't be confused with someone else's.

```
acme_checks/
├── __init__.py
└── conf/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── pointblank/
        ├── checks/
        │   └── acme/
        │       ├── ids.yaml
        │       └── emails.yaml
        └── thresholds/
            └── acme/
                └── no_failures.yaml
```

The `conf/` directory needs an `__init__.py` (which can be empty), since Hydra finds the
directory by importing it.

## Write the Collections

A check collection starts with a `# @package checks.<name>` header. Include the name of your
package or organization in `<name>`: two selected collections with the same name are an error.

```yaml
# acme_checks/conf/pointblank/checks/acme/ids.yaml
# @package checks.acme_ids
steps:
  - col_vals_not_null:
      columns: ${vars.id_column}
  - rows_distinct:
      columns_subset: ${vars.id_column}
```

Use `${vars.<name>}` for anything that differs between the tables the checks will be used on,
and list those variables in your package's documentation. A config that selects the collection
has to define each of them.

Options for the other groups use the header of their group (see the
[table of config groups](yaml-reference.qmd#config-groups)):

```yaml
# acme_checks/conf/pointblank/thresholds/acme/no_failures.yaml
# @package thresholds
critical: 1
```

## Include a Check Written in Python

A collection can use a function from your package by its import path. Write a function that
returns the check, with the settings of the check as its parameters:

```python
# acme_checks/checks.py
import pointblank as pb


def min_rows(n: int):
    """Make a check that passes when the table has at least `n` rows."""

    def check(tbl) -> bool:
        return pb.get_row_count(tbl) >= n

    return check
```

In the collection, give the function as the `_target_` of the `expr` of a `specially` step, with
its arguments as the other keys:

```yaml
# acme_checks/conf/pointblank/checks/acme/size.yaml
# @package checks.acme_size
steps:
  - specially:
      expr:
        _target_: acme_checks.checks.min_rows
        n: ${vars.min_rows}
```

Anyone who selects the collection runs this code, without having to allow it.

## Register the Config Tree

Add an entry point to the `hydra.lernaplugins` group in `pyproject.toml`, with `pkg:` followed
by the import path of the config directory. Depend on `pointblank[hydra]`, which installs what's
needed to find the entry point.

```toml
[project]
name = "acme-checks"
dependencies = ["pointblank[hydra]"]

[project.entry-points."hydra.lernaplugins"]
acme-checks = "pkg:acme_checks.conf"
```

Check that your build includes the YAML files in the wheel and in the source distribution.

## Try It Before Installing

To test the config tree without building the package, pass its directory with `--config-dir`:

```bash
pb compose pointblank/tbl=small_table 'pointblank/checks=[acme/ids]' +vars.id_column=a \
  --config-dir acme_checks/conf
```

## Select the Options from Another Project

With the package installed, its options are selected like any others, by their path within the
group:

```yaml
defaults:
  - override /pointblank/thresholds: acme/no_failures
  - override /pointblank/checks:
      - acme/ids
      - acme/emails
  - _self_

vars:
  id_column: customer_id
  email_column: email

tbl: customers.csv
```

If an installed package and the project's own directory both have an option at the same path,
the one from the package is used. Keeping your options in a directory of their own, as above,
avoids that.
